## Objective

Identify and account for vessels that GFW misclassifies in the raw VP and AFE
pulls, following the hybrid approach in `planning/vessel_filtering_plan.qmd`:

- a **decisions file** (`references/vessel_decisions.csv`, tracked in git) is
  the only file edited by hand; together with `references/vessel_removals.csv`
  it generates the **MMSI crosswalk** that classifies every record
- a **screen** of the raw data produces review lists
- the **GFW vessel-identity API** and **NOAA GARFO permit lists** supply evidence

This is the analyst's step: it needs the GARFO permit lists and the API
caches, which are not in git, and it is the only step that writes to
`references/`. `04_classify_aggregate.qmd` then applies the crosswalk to every
record and builds the two analysis sets, **Strict** (GFW's unprocessed labels)
and **Primary** (the verified classification), from tracked files alone.
Re-render this file before 04 whenever an input in `references/` changes;
04 stops if the crosswalk is out of date.

Two separate problems are handled:

- **Hull identity** -- is the vessel a fishing vessel at all? GFW types some
  fishing vessels OTHER (`OTHER_NON_FISHING` from pipeline v5), GEAR,
  PASSENGER or, in v5, `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` (false negatives) and some
  non-fishing vessels FISHING (false positives).
- **Activity** -- is a fishing vessel fishing at this moment? Charter guard and
  survey work by fishing hulls is classed as fishing by GFW (false positives).
  This depends on dates, so crosswalk rows carry a validity window.

## How to use this workflow

Every run rebuilds everything from tracked inputs, so the outputs depend only
on the raw pull, the GARFO files, the API cache and these files:

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `references/vessel_removals.csv` | Ørsted charter and other known removals (input) |
| `references/orsted_fv_survey_dates_*.csv` | Ørsted survey trips by vessel, as delivered (input; every matching file is read) |
| `references/orsted_survey_vessels.csv` | Survey-file vessel names → MMSI (input) |
| `references/vessel_decisions.csv` | Your hull and activity decisions (input, edited by hand) |
| `references/vessel_gear.csv` | Your gear corrections (input, edited by hand) |
| `references/garfo_permit_codes.csv` | GARFO permit code meanings (input) |
| `references/vessel_crosswalk_{pipeline}.csv` | Generated each run from the removals, survey dates and decisions -- do not edit |
| `references/vessel_permit_groups_{pipeline}.csv` | Generated each run: GARFO permit group per MMSI, for 04's dual-permit check -- do not edit |
| `references/fishing_roster_{pipeline}.csv` | Written **once** per GFW pipeline version with `-P write_roster:true`: every MMSI that counted as fishing in that pull -- never edit or regenerate |
| `data/processed/vessel_review/{pipeline}/vessel_review.csv` | Generated each run: hull/activity candidates, evidence and a suggested decision |
| `data/processed/vessel_review/{pipeline}/gear_review.csv` | Generated each run: fishing vessels whose gear needs checking, with a suggested gear class |

Each pass:

1. **Run with the API off** (the default). Check the list sizes and screening
   thresholds.
2. **Run once with the APIs on**: render with
   `-P run_gfw_api:true -P run_psix_api:true`, or set both in the header.
   Lookups are cached in `data/raw/vessel_evidence/` (GFW identity lookups
   in its `{pipeline}/` folder, PSIX lookups shared), so each Vessel ID, hull
   ID and call sign is queried once; set them back to `false` afterwards. The
   PSIX lookups need the GFW evidence (they run only for vessels that reach
   the review sheet), so turn PSIX on in the same run as the GFW API or after
   it.
3. **Review** the two sheets. Their first columns are a suggestion in the same
   layout as the matching input file (`vessel_review.csv` →
   `vessel_decisions.csv`; `gear_review.csv` → `vessel_gear.csv`). For each row
   you decide on, correct the suggestion if needed and set `decision` to
   `accept` or `reject`. Leave `decision` blank to skip a row. On the first
   run against a new GFW pipeline version, list 5 of the review sheet holds
   the vessels that counted as fishing in the previous version but that GFW
   no longer types FISHING (the roster check, Phase 1): accept to keep one in
   Primary, reject to let the new label stand.
4. **Re-run.** The run first copies every row with a `decision` from the two
   sheets into their input files, then regenerates the crosswalk and both
   sheets, so decided vessels drop off. You can also edit the input files
   directly.
5. **Commit `vessel_decisions.csv` and `vessel_gear.csv`** after each review
   session; they are the record of every decision.

Hull and activity decisions are kept separate from gear corrections, so a
vessel's gear can be fixed without touching its charter exclusion (e.g. a
removal-list charter vessel whose GFW gear is wrong).

If you open the review sheet in Excel, import it with every column as Text
(Data → From Text/CSV) and save as CSV UTF-8. Opened directly, Excel rewrites
dates (e.g. `2024-04-26` → `4/26/2024`) and long IDs, and the crosswalk
validation then stops the run.

## Libraries and shared code

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(gfwr)

source("r/paths.R")
source("r/gfw_helpers.R")
source("r/vessel_helpers.R")
source("r/review_helpers.R") # the review's own functions

# Quarto parameters (header); `params` is read-only while rendering. Run chunk
# by chunk (Positron, RStudio), `params` is missing or left over from another
# session, so the header is read from this file directly instead
qparams <- if (isTRUE(getOption("knitr.in.progress"))) params else {
  hdr <- knitr::knit_params(readLines(
    file.path(root, "r/03_review_vessels.qmd"), warn = FALSE))
  lapply(hdr, function(p) p$value)
}
paths       <- gfw_paths_with(qparams)
run_gfw_api <- isTRUE(qparams$run_gfw_api)
message("GFW identity API lookups are ", if (run_gfw_api) "ON" else "OFF")
run_psix_api <- isTRUE(qparams$run_psix_api)
message("USCG PSIX lookups are ", if (run_psix_api) "ON" else "OFF")
```

## Parameters

```{r}
# date of the raw pull (pull_info.csv, written by 01_pull_gfw.qmd)
pull_date <- read_pull_date(paths)
pull_date

# screening thresholds -- record any change in the methods
screen <- list(
  min_s3_hours     = 50,   # charter screen: minimum Stage 3 VP hours
  min_lease_share  = 0.25, # charter screen: share of hours inside SFW/RWF/SRW
  max_prior_hours  = 0,    # charter screen: Stage 1-2 hours for a "no history" burst
  min_lease_shift  = 0.25, # charter screen: rise in lease share, Stage 1-2 to 3
  # charter speed check (v5 pulls on; D-072): share of Stage 3 AFE hours on
  # days with a mean speed below 4 kn, and the least AFE to judge it on
  speed_min_afe_h  = 20,   # speed check: fewer AFE hours with a speed -> "too few hours"
  standby_min_lt4  = 0.75, # speed check: at least this share below 4 kn -> "standby-like"
  underway_max_lt4 = 0.50, # speed check: less than this share below 4 kn -> "underway"
  fp_max_days      = 30,   # FP screen: short foreign-flag visit, active days
  fp_min_h_day     = 12,   # FP screen: hours per active day
  length_tolerance = 0.15, # GARFO vs GFW registry length agreement (share)
  max_resolve_hulls = 3,   # most GARFO hulls a name can match and still be resolved by length
  oa_bundle_min    = 5     # open-access commercial permits that mark a party-boat bundle
)

api_batch_size <- 20 # Vessel IDs per API request

# last day the Ørsted survey-date files cover (r/vessel_helpers.R); move it
# there when a new file arrives
survey_dates_through
```

## Read raw data

```{r}
# read_gfw() (r/gfw_helpers.R) types the hours, derives Year Month and
# Development Stage, and snaps Lat/Lon to the 0.01 degree cell_id; records
# after analysis_end are dropped
vp  <- read_gfw(paths$raw_vp)  |> in_analysis_window()
afe <- read_gfw(paths$raw_afe) |> in_analysis_window()

stopifnot("records with no development stage" =
            !anyNA(vp$`Development Stage`) && !anyNA(afe$`Development Stage`))

total_vp  <- sum(vp$hours)
total_afe <- sum(afe$hours)
```

```{r}
# GFW labels per MMSI as of this pull (most frequent, in case of a split)
gfw_labels <- gfw_labels_of(vp, afe)
```

```{r}
# lease flag per grid cell (cell centre inside SFW, RWF or SRW)
grid <- st_read(paths$grid, quiet = TRUE)

leases <- paths$leases |>
  map(\(p) st_read(p, quiet = TRUE) |> st_transform(st_crs(grid)) |> st_union()) |>
  reduce(st_union)

cell_lease <- tibble(
  cell_id  = grid$cell_id,
  in_lease = lengths(st_intersects(st_centroid(st_geometry(grid)), leases)) > 0)

stopifnot("records outside the fishnet grid" =
            all(c(vp$cell_id, afe$cell_id) %in% cell_lease$cell_id))
```

## Phase 1: Decisions and the crosswalk

The crosswalk has one row per MMSI per validity period. A record is matched to
the row whose `valid_from`–`valid_to` window contains its date (blank =
open-ended). Records with no matching row keep GFW's label. Windows for one
MMSI must not overlap, so a fishing hull GFW missed that also took a charter
needs two rows: one before the charter (`activity_excluded = FALSE`) and one
for the charter (`TRUE`).

| Column | Values |
|---|---|
| `MMSI` | 9 digits; any format for `gear_marker`; other malformed MMSIs exactly as in the GFW pull |
| `valid_from`, `valid_to` | ISO dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`); blank = open-ended |
| `hull_class` | `fishing` / `non_fishing` / `gear_marker` / `unknown` |
| `activity_excluded` | `TRUE` = records in the window are not fishing (charter work) |
| `Identified_By`, `evidence_ref`, `Notes` | Where the decision came from |
| `gfw_vessel_type`, `gfw_gear_type`, `pull_date` | GFW's labels when the decision was made |

`vessel_decisions.csv` has the same columns plus `decision` (`accept` /
`reject`) and `decided_on`. Every crosswalk row is treated as verified: accept
a suggestion only after checking it (MarineTraffic, CGMIX PSIX, the operator's
website), and record the check in `evidence_ref`. The crosswalk is built as:

- **Removal-list rows.** Charter vessels (`Scope == "stages_2_3"`) become
  fishing hulls with an activity exclusion from the start of Stage 2;
  `all_stages` vessels become non-fishing hulls.
- **Survey-date rows.** Ørsted's survey trip lists
  (`references/orsted_fv_survey_dates_*.csv`) give the actual survey dates.
  Each vessel name is mapped to an MMSI through
  `references/orsted_survey_vessels.csv`. A trip's Departure Date is the day
  its gear was set and its Return Date the day it was retrieved, so only
  those two days are excluded; the soak days between them count as fishing
  (D-073). A vessel's set and haul days on consecutive dates are merged into
  one window.
  For each survey vessel these windows replace its open-ended removal-list
  row, so its records between surveys -- and before its first listed trip --
  count as fishing. The files cover trips through `survey_dates_through`
  (2026-08-31), which is also where the analysis window ends, so no survey
  vessel's records fall after the files' coverage. Two kinds of vessel keep their removal-list
  row instead: those listed as `Safety`, whose guard and scout work the survey
  files do not date, and any MMSI with a decision.
- **Precedence.** A decision replaces survey-date and removal-list rows; survey-date
  rows replace removal-list rows.
- **Accepted decisions.** Any decision for an MMSI on the removal list
  replaces that vessel's removal-list rows -- this is how to give a charter
  vessel its real charter dates. A `reject` for a removal-list MMSI removes
  it from the crosswalk.
- **Rejected decisions** add no row: GFW's label stands, and the vessel no
  longer appears in the review sheet.

Gear is not part of the crosswalk. It is corrected separately in
`references/vessel_gear.csv` (see *Gear corrections* below), so fixing a
vessel's gear never touches its hull or charter treatment.

### Collect decisions from the last review sheets

```{r}
review_path      <- file.path(paths$review, "vessel_review.csv")
gear_review_path <- file.path(paths$review, "gear_review.csv")

decisions   <- collect_marked(review_path, paths$decisions, decision_cols, paths$pipeline)
gear_inputs <- collect_marked(gear_review_path, paths$gear, gear_cols, paths$pipeline)

count(decisions, decision)
count(gear_inputs, decision)
```

### Build and validate the crosswalk

```{r}
# removal list, survey dates and accepted decisions -> crosswalk
# (build_crosswalk() in r/vessel_helpers.R; 04 rebuilds it the same way)
cw_out <- build_crosswalk(paths, decisions, gfw_labels, pull_date)
cw     <- type_crosswalk(cw_out, gfw_labels, source = paths$decisions)

write_csv(cw_out, paths$crosswalk, na = "")

count(cw, hull_class, activity_excluded)
```

### Gear corrections

`references/vessel_gear.csv` overrides GFW's gear for the records of a vessel
inside each row's `valid_from`–`valid_to` window (blank = open-ended). An
`accept` row sets `gear_class` (`MOBILE` / `FIXED` / `POLE_AND_LINE` /
`UNRESOLVED`); a `reject` row records that GFW's gear was checked and kept, so
the vessel leaves the gear review sheet. `basis` says where the gear came from
(e.g. `analyst knowledge`, `GARFO permit`, `GFW registry`). Every record's
gear class is then the accepted correction if there is one, otherwise GFW's
`Gear Type` through the gear map in `r/gfw_helpers.R`.

```{r}
gear <- validate_gear(gear_inputs, source = paths$gear)

count(gear, gear_class, basis)
```

### The previous version's fishing roster

GFW relabels vessels between pipeline versions. Most vessels counted as
fishing are in Strict and Primary only because GFW types them FISHING, with
no crosswalk row, so a retype would drop them unseen. On a run against a new
version this step reads the roster written for the previous one
(`references/fishing_roster_{version}.csv`, Phase 5) and compares every
roster MMSI with this pull (`roster_changes()` in `r/vessel_helpers.R`;
`planning/gfw_pipeline_v5_plan.qmd`, Sections 2.7 and 3.6):

- **type** -- GFW's vessel type changed. Unless the MMSI already has a
  crosswalk row, a vessel that was in the previous Primary set goes on list 5
  of the review sheet (Phase 2).
- **gear_class** -- the analysis gear class its records get changed. Unless
  it has a gear correction, it goes on the gear review sheet.
- **missing** -- no records in this pull's analysis window; reported in
  Phase 6.

A change is **protected** when an existing decision settles it (a crosswalk
row for a type change, a gear correction for a gear-class change); protected
changes are listed but need no review. On a run against the version the
newest roster describes (v4 now), there is nothing to compare and the step is
skipped.

```{r}
prev_roster_path <- previous_roster_path(paths$roster, paths$pipeline)

if (is.null(prev_roster_path)) {
  prev_roster   <- NULL
  roster_chk    <- NULL
  prev_pipeline <- NA_character_
  message("No roster of an earlier pipeline version than ", paths$pipeline,
          "; the roster check is skipped")
} else {
  prev_roster   <- read_chr(prev_roster_path)
  prev_pipeline <- unique(prev_roster$pipeline)
  message("Roster check against ", prev_roster_path, " (", nrow(prev_roster), " MMSIs)")

  # the gear class each MMSI's records get in this pull, weighted by hours,
  # computed as build_fishing_roster() did for the roster
  gear_now <- bind_rows(classify(vp, cw, gear), classify(afe, cw, gear)) |>
    filter(!is.na(MMSI)) |>
    count(MMSI, gear_class, wt = hours) |>
    group_by(MMSI) |>
    slice_max(n, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    ungroup()

  roster_chk <- roster_changes(prev_roster, gfw_labels, gear_now, cw, gear)

  # changes by kind, for vessels in and out of the previous Primary set, with
  # their hours in the previous version
  roster_chk |>
    group_by(change, protected, in_primary) |>
    summarise(vessels = n(), vp_hours_old = round(sum(vp_hours_old)),
              afe_hours_old = round(sum(afe_hours_old)), .groups = "drop")
}
```

```{r}
# how the previous Primary set's type changes moved, unprotected ones only
if (!is.null(roster_chk)) {
  roster_chk |>
    filter(change == "type", in_primary, !protected) |>
    count(type_old, type_new, name = "vessels", sort = TRUE)
}
```

## Phase 2: Screen the raw data

### Per-MMSI profile

```{r}
profiles <- profile_mmsi(vp, afe, cell_lease, gfw_labels)

# speed check for the charter screen (D-072): v5 pulls on only. A vessel
# with no Stage 3 AFE on a day with a speed gets 0 hours ("too few hours");
# on a pull without speed every column stays NA and the check is skipped.
speed_prof <- afe_speed_profile(vp, afe)
profiles <- if (is.null(speed_prof)) {
  message("No Speed field in this pull: the charter speed check is skipped")
  mutate(profiles, afe_speed_h = NA_real_, afe_lt2 = NA_real_, afe_lt4 = NA_real_,
         afe_median_kn = NA_real_)
} else {
  profiles |>
    left_join(speed_prof, by = "MMSI") |>
    mutate(afe_speed_h = coalesce(afe_speed_h, 0))
}
profiles <- mutate(profiles, speed_class = speed_class(afe_speed_h, afe_lt4, screen))

nrow(profiles)
```

### GARFO permit matches

The GARFO permit lists (`data/raw/vessel_evidence/registries/`, one file per
permit year plus the HMS/tuna file) identify vessels only by name, permit
number and hull ID. Neither permit number nor hull ID appears in AIS, so the
only link is the vessel name. Names collide (many GARFO names belong to more
than one hull, and placeholders such as UNNAMED and SKIFF are common), so a
name match is only a lead:

| `garfo_match` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `unique_years` | One GARFO hull and one US-flag MMSI share the name, and a permit year falls within the MMSI's AIS activity |
| `unique_no_year_overlap` | Unique, but no permit year overlaps the AIS activity |
| `ambiguous` | The name belongs to several hulls, or to several MMSIs active at the same time. MMSIs sharing a name whose activity never overlaps (a changed MMSI, or a replacement vessel with the same name) are not counted as ambiguous (`garfo_mmsi_sequence`); the permit years must still overlap the MMSI's activity |
| `none` | No match |

Phase 4 adds a length check once GFW registry lengths are available. A name
match is only a suggestion. To confirm one, look up the hull ID in
the USCG PSIX search on CGMIX (numeric hull IDs are USCG official numbers) and
check that the vessel's call sign matches the AIS call sign, then record the
hull ID in `evidence_ref`. State-registered hull IDs (e.g. `MS6930PP`) cannot
be linked to a call sign this way.

Only vessel fields are read; owner names, telephone numbers and addresses are
never loaded.

```{r}
garfo_files <- list.files(paths$registries,
                          pattern = "^garfo.*[.]csv$", full.names = TRUE)

garfo_read  <- map(garfo_files, read_garfo)
garfo_all   <- map(garfo_read, "permits") |> list_rbind()
garfo_codes <- map(garfo_read, "codes") |> list_rbind()

# rows broken in the source file (e.g. shifted fields) have no valid year
malformed <- with(garfo_all, is.na(permit_year) | !between(permit_year, 2000, 2100) |
                    is.na(hull_id) | is.na(vessel_name))
message("GARFO rows read: ", nrow(garfo_all), "; malformed rows dropped: ", sum(malformed))

garfo_all   <- garfo_all[!malformed, ]
garfo_codes <- semi_join(garfo_codes, garfo_all, by = c("file", "permit", "permit_year"))
```

### GARFO permit codes

Permit codes are fishery-specific. The meanings live in
`references/garfo_permit_codes.csv`, one row per fishery and code, with
`permit_type` (`commercial` / `for_hire` / `recreational` / `unknown`), an
optional `gear_hint` (`FIXED` / `MOBILE`), a `description`, and the `basis`
and `source` for each mapping (NOAA Fisheries permit pages). Category 2 is
charter/party in every fishery that has one (bluefish, black sea bass, scup,
summer flounder, tilefish, lobster, squid/mackerel/butterfish), and tilefish 3
is the private recreational permit; otherwise codes are fishery-specific (e.g.
squid/mackerel/butterfish 3 = incidental catch, 4 = Atlantic mackerel open
access). Codes missing from the table are listed below and treated as
`unknown`.

For commercial permits, `open_access` marks those anyone can obtain, and
`oa_directed` separates open-access permits for a directed fishery (e.g.
spiny dogfish, bluefish, tilefish, Handgear B, HMS General) from incidental
ones (monkfish E, squid/butterfish incidental, multispecies J). The HMS file's
`CML CHB ENDORSEMENT = Y` (a charter/headboat permit endorsed for commercial
sale) is read as an extra open-access commercial code.

```{r}
permit_codes <- read_csv(paths$permit_codes, col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
                         na = "")

unmapped <- garfo_codes |>
  count(fishery, code, name = "permit_years") |>
  anti_join(permit_codes, by = c("fishery", "code"))

if (nrow(unmapped) > 0) {
  warning(nrow(unmapped), " GARFO codes are missing from ", paths$permit_codes,
          " and are treated as unknown", call. = FALSE)
}
unmapped

# permit type and gear hints per permit-year
permit_flags <- garfo_codes |>
  left_join(permit_codes, by = c("fishery", "code")) |>
  mutate(fc = paste0(fishery, ":", code),
         comm_oa = permit_type %in% "commercial" & open_access %in% "TRUE") |>
  group_by(file, permit, permit_year) |>
  summarise(
    # commercial permits that are not open access (limited access, moratorium)
    commercial_la = any(permit_type %in% "commercial" & !comm_oa),
    commercial_oa = any(comm_oa),
    for_hire      = any(permit_type %in% "for_hire"),
    recreational  = any(permit_type %in% "recreational"),
    fixed_hint    = any(gear_hint %in% "FIXED"),
    mobile_hint   = any(gear_hint %in% "MOBILE"),
    oa_permits    = paste(fc[comm_oa], collapse = "|"),
    oa_directed_permits = paste(fc[comm_oa & oa_directed %in% "TRUE"], collapse = "|"),
    categories    = paste(fc, collapse = "; "),
    .groups = "drop")

garfo <- garfo_all |>
  left_join(permit_flags, by = c("file", "permit", "permit_year")) |>
  mutate(across(c(commercial_la, commercial_oa, for_hire, recreational, fixed_hint, mobile_hint),
                \(x) coalesce(x, FALSE)),
         fixed_hint   = fixed_hint | coalesce(trap_limit > 0, FALSE),
         nkey         = norm_name(vessel_name),
         hull_is_uscg = str_detect(hull_id, "^[0-9]+$")) |>
  filter(!nkey %in% placeholder_names, nchar(nkey) >= 3)

garfo |>
  count(source, commercial_la, commercial_oa, for_hire, recreational)
```

```{r}
# AIS names per MMSI; GARFO vessels are US, so match US- or unflagged MMSIs
ais_names <- bind_rows(vp, afe) |>
  filter(!is.na(MMSI), !is.na(`Vessel Name`), Flag %in% c("USA", NA)) |>
  distinct(MMSI, `Vessel Name`) |>
  mutate(nkey = norm_name(`Vessel Name`)) |>
  filter(!nkey %in% placeholder_names, nchar(nkey) >= 3) |>
  distinct(MMSI, nkey)

# MMSIs sharing a name whose AIS activity never overlaps are one vessel that
# changed MMSI, or a replacement vessel given the same name (e.g. CAILYN &
# MAREN 2021-2025, then CAILYN AND MAREN II from late 2025). Either way they
# do not make the name ambiguous; the permit-year check still has to tie the
# GARFO hull to the right MMSI. An MMSI with no profile counts as overlapping.
ais_name_counts <- ais_names |>
  left_join(select(profiles, MMSI, first, last), by = "MMSI") |>
  arrange(nkey, first) |>
  group_by(nkey) |>
  summarise(mmsi_with_name = n_distinct(MMSI),
            mmsi_overlap   = anyNA(first) ||
              any(lead(as.numeric(first)) <= cummax(as.numeric(last)), na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

name_counts <- full_join(
  garfo |> group_by(nkey) |> summarise(hulls_with_name = n_distinct(hull_id)),
  ais_name_counts,
  by = "nkey")

garfo_matches <- ais_names |>
  inner_join(garfo, by = "nkey", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  left_join(name_counts, by = "nkey") |>
  left_join(select(profiles, MMSI, first, last), by = "MMSI")

garfo_by_mmsi <- garfo_matches |> group_by(MMSI) |> summarise_garfo(screen$oa_bundle_min)
garfo_by_hull <- garfo_matches |> group_by(MMSI, hull_id) |> summarise_garfo(screen$oa_bundle_min) |>
  select(-hull_id)

# drop any GARFO columns from an earlier run of this chunk, so re-running it
# interactively does not leave suffixed duplicates (garfo_match.x, .y)
profiles <- profiles |>
  select(-any_of(setdiff(names(garfo_by_mmsi), "MMSI"))) |>
  left_join(garfo_by_mmsi, by = "MMSI") |>
  mutate(garfo_match = coalesce(garfo_match, "none"))
```

How often does a name match succeed for vessels whose fishing status is
already known? US-flag vessels GFW types FISHING, and the fishing hulls in the
crosswalk, set the expectation; matches among non-FISHING vessels are the
leads.

```{r}
profiles |>
  filter(flag %in% "USA") |>
  mutate(group = case_when(
    MMSI %in% cw$MMSI[cw$hull_class == "fishing"] ~ "crosswalk fishing hull",
    gfw_vessel_type %in% "FISHING"                ~ "GFW FISHING",
    TRUE                                          ~ "GFW non-FISHING")) |>
  count(group, garfo_match) |>
  group_by(group) |>
  mutate(share = round(n / sum(n), 3)) |>
  ungroup()
```

### Candidate lists

Each list excludes vessels already in the crosswalk or in the decisions file.

1. **Missed fishing vessels** -- typed other than FISHING, and either US-flag
   (with or without a call sign; small sport fishing boats often have none)
   or with a unique, year-overlapping GARFO name match. This whole pool is
   looked up in the GFW API, but only vessels with evidence reach the review
   sheet (Phase 4).
2. **Charter activity** -- typed FISHING with a lease-concentrated Stage 3:
   either no Stage 1–2 history (a burst), or a lease share that rose from
   Stages 1–2 to Stage 3 (catches established vessels that took a charter, the
   *Virginia Wave* blind spot). On pulls with a speed field (v5 on), each
   candidate also gets a **speed check** (D-072): the share of its Stage 3
   AFE on days with a mean speed below 2 and 4 kn, and a `speed_class`.
   Safety and guard vessels standing by a construction site are slow
   (`standby-like`); a fishing vessel that simply works the lease areas tows
   at fishing speed (`underway`). The flag rule is unchanged, so the screen
   still finds every candidate; the speed check informs the decision.
3. **Non-fishing vessels typed FISHING** -- research or survey names, short
   intense foreign-flag visits, or foreign-flag vessels whose gear is
   unresolved (`INCONCLUSIVE` in v4; generic `FISHING` and the rest of the
   `UNRESOLVED` gear class in any version, since v5 dropped `INCONCLUSIVE`).
4. **Gear markers and malformed MMSIs** -- call signs holding battery levels
   (e.g. ONWA33NT, likely AIS net buoys), or MMSIs that are not 9 digits
   (some are vessels with misconfigured transponders, e.g. ROYAL with call sign
   WDD3653, so these are suggested as `unknown` for review).
5. **Roster label changes** (a run against a new pipeline version only) --
   vessels in the previous version's Primary set that GFW has retyped, with no
   crosswalk row and no decision made against this version. Unlike list 1,
   every one is reviewed, evidence or not. A vessel on list 5 is left off
   list 1, so it appears once. A decision from an earlier version that added
   no crosswalk row (a `reject`) does not keep a vessel off list 5: it was
   made against the old label.

```{r}
open_profiles <- profiles |> filter(!MMSI %in% c(cw$MMSI, decisions$MMSI))

# list 5 first, so list 1 can leave its vessels out
roster_type <- if (is.null(roster_chk)) {
  # no roster check on this run: an empty table, so list 5 is empty
  tibble(MMSI = character(), type_old = character(), gear_old = character(),
         vp_hours_old = numeric(), afe_hours_old = numeric())
} else {
  roster_chk |> filter(change == "type", in_primary, !protected)
}
decided_now <- decisions$MMSI[decisions$gfw_pipeline %in% paths$pipeline]

cand_roster <- profiles |>
  filter(MMSI %in% roster_type$MMSI, !MMSI %in% c(cw$MMSI, decided_now)) |>
  left_join(select(roster_type, MMSI, type_old, gear_old, vp_hours_old, afe_hours_old),
            by = "MMSI") |>
  mutate(list = "5_roster_label_change",
         reason = paste0(prev_pipeline, " ", type_old, "/", coalesce(gear_old, "none"),
                         " -> ", paths$pipeline, " ", gfw_vessel_type, "/",
                         coalesce(gfw_gear_type, "none"), "; ", prev_pipeline,
                         " hours VP ", round(vp_hours_old, 1), ", AFE ",
                         round(afe_hours_old, 1))) |>
  # keep the previous version's AFE hours to order list 5 by: GFW computes
  # fishing effort only for vessels it treats as fishing, so a retyped vessel
  # has next to none in this pull
  select(-type_old, -gear_old, -vp_hours_old)

cand_missed <- open_profiles |>
  filter(!MMSI %in% cand_roster$MMSI) |>
  filter(!gfw_vessel_type %in% "FISHING", mmsi_valid,
         flag %in% "USA" | garfo_match == "unique_years") |>
  mutate(list = "1_missed_fishing",
         reason = case_when(
           garfo_match == "unique_years" ~ "typed non-FISHING; unique GARFO name match",
           !is.na(call_sign)             ~ "typed non-FISHING; US flag with call sign",
           TRUE                          ~ "typed non-FISHING; US flag, no call sign"))

cand_charter <- charter_screen(open_profiles, screen) |>
  filter(gfw_vessel_type %in% "FISHING", charter_flag) |>
  mutate(list = "2_charter_activity",
         reason = case_when(
           burst & shift ~ "no Stage 1-2 history and lease share rose",
           burst         ~ "no Stage 1-2 history; lease-concentrated Stage 3",
           TRUE          ~ "lease share rose from Stage 1-2 to Stage 3"))

cand_nonfishing <- open_profiles |>
  filter(gfw_vessel_type %in% "FISHING") |>
  mutate(research = str_detect(names, "\\bNOAA\\b|^R/V|RESEARCH|SURVEY"),
         visit    = !flag %in% "USA" & days <= screen$fp_max_days &
                    h_day >= screen$fp_min_h_day,
         # v5 has no INCONCLUSIVE gear; the UNRESOLVED class covers it, generic
         # FISHING and any other code the gear map does not resolve
         inconcl  = !flag %in% "USA" & gear_class_of(gfw_gear_type) == "UNRESOLVED") |>
  filter(research | visit | inconcl) |>
  mutate(list = "3_nonfishing_typed_fishing",
         reason = case_when(research ~ "research or survey name",
                            visit    ~ "short, intense foreign-flag visit",
                            TRUE     ~ paste0("foreign flag with unresolved gear (",
                                              gfw_gear_type, ")")))

cand_marker <- open_profiles |>
  filter(!mmsi_valid | battery_call_sign) |>
  mutate(list = "4_gear_marker",
         reason = if_else(battery_call_sign, "call sign holds a battery level",
                          "MMSI is not 9 digits"))

candidates <- bind_rows(cand_missed, cand_charter, cand_nonfishing, cand_marker,
                        cand_roster) |>
  select(list, reason, MMSI, names, flag, call_sign, gfw_vessel_type,
         gfw_gear_type, vp_hours, s1, s2, s3, afe_hours, days, h_day,
         lease_share, lease_share_s12, lease_share_s3, s3_lease_first,
         s3_lease_last, first, last, any_of(c("burst", "shift", "afe_hours_old")),
         afe_speed_h, afe_lt2, afe_lt4, afe_median_kn, speed_class,
         starts_with("garfo_"), hull_is_uscg) |>
  # the speed check is for charter candidates only (D-072)
  mutate(across(c(afe_speed_h, afe_lt2, afe_lt4, afe_median_kn, speed_class),
                \(x) if_else(list == "2_charter_activity", x, NA))) |>
  arrange(list, desc(vp_hours))

candidates |>
  group_by(list) |>
  summarise(vessels = n(), vp_hours = sum(vp_hours), afe_hours = sum(afe_hours))
```

### How well does the charter screen find known charters?

The vessels Ørsted confirmed are the best available ground truth. The share
the screen flags is its recall; vessels it misses show what it cannot see.

```{r}
# Ørsted sources: its charter lists and emails, survey-date files and the SFW
# PSO/PAM report (older rows say orsted_list)
orsted_charters <- cw |>
  filter(str_detect(Identified_By, regex("orsted|PSO PAM", ignore_case = TRUE)),
         activity_excluded) |>
  distinct(MMSI)

screen_recall <- charter_screen(profiles, screen) |>
  inner_join(orsted_charters, by = "MMSI")

screen_recall |>
  summarise(vessels = n(), flagged = sum(charter_flag),
            recall = round(mean(charter_flag), 2))

screen_recall |>
  filter(!charter_flag) |>
  select(MMSI, names, s1, s2, s3, lease_share, lease_share_s12, lease_share_s3)

# the speed check's calibration, re-checked on every run with speed (D-072):
# confirmed safety vessels should be standby-like. The profile covers all of
# Stage 3, not only the charter window, so a vessel that also fished in
# Stage 3 can come out mixed. Survey vessels are left out: survey work tows
# gear or steams between stations, so it is not slow.
if (!all(is.na(profiles$speed_class))) {
  safety_mmsi <- cw |>
    filter(activity_excluded, str_detect(coalesce(Operation, ""), regex("safety", ignore_case = TRUE))) |>
    distinct(MMSI)
  profiles |>
    semi_join(orsted_charters, by = "MMSI") |>
    semi_join(safety_mmsi, by = "MMSI") |>
    count(speed_class, name = "safety_vessels")
}
```

### Gear review candidates

Fishing vessels are those GFW types FISHING plus the crosswalk's fishing hulls
(removal-list charter vessels and accepted missed fishing vessels). One of
them goes on the gear review sheet, until it has a row in
`vessel_gear.csv`, if:

- it is on the **removal list** -- every removal-list fishing vessel is
  reviewed, because GFW's gear can be wrong even when it is resolved (e.g.
  CAILYN AND MAREN, a lobster trap boat GFW labels `POLE_AND_LINE`);
- GFW's gear is **unresolved** (`FISHING`, `INCONCLUSIVE`, `OTHER`, ...);
- or a unique GARFO match's permits **disagree** with GFW's gear class;
- or, on a run against a new pipeline version, its **gear class changed**
  since the previous version's roster and no gear correction covers it (the
  roster check, Phase 1). This catches a change from one specific class to
  another (e.g. FIXED to MOBILE), which none of the rules above would. A
  roster vessel GFW has retyped away from FISHING is on list 5 of the review
  sheet instead; like an accepted list-1 vessel, it reaches this sheet once
  its decision makes it a crosswalk fishing hull.

```{r}
removal_mmsi <- read_chr(paths$removals)$MMSI

fishing_mmsi <- union(profiles$MMSI[profiles$gfw_vessel_type %in% "FISHING"],
                      cw$MMSI[cw$hull_class == "fishing"]) |>
  setdiff(cw$MMSI[cw$hull_class != "fishing"])

# gear-class changes since the previous roster that no correction covers, and
# the note that says what changed
roster_gear_note <- if (is.null(roster_chk)) {
  tibble(MMSI = character(), roster_gear_change = character())
} else {
  roster_chk |>
    filter(change == "gear_class", !protected) |>
    transmute(MMSI, roster_gear_change = paste0(
      "gear class changed since ", prev_pipeline, ": ", class_old, " -> ", class_new))
}
roster_gear_mmsi <- roster_gear_note$MMSI

gear_candidates <- profiles |>
  filter(MMSI %in% fishing_mmsi, !MMSI %in% gear_inputs$MMSI) |>
  mutate(gfw_class       = gear_class_of(gfw_gear_type),
         garfo_hint      = if_else(garfo_match == "unique_years", garfo_gear_hint, NA_character_),
         on_removal_list = MMSI %in% removal_mmsi,
         unresolved      = gfw_class == "UNRESOLVED",
         garfo_conflict  = !unresolved & !is.na(garfo_hint) & garfo_hint != gfw_class,
         # unprotected gear-class changes since the previous roster (none on a
         # run without a roster check)
         roster_gear     = MMSI %in% roster_gear_mmsi) |>
  filter(on_removal_list | unresolved | garfo_conflict | roster_gear) |>
  left_join(roster_gear_note, by = "MMSI") |>
  mutate(gear_reason = str_remove(paste0(
    if_else(on_removal_list, "removal list; ", ""),
    if_else(unresolved, "GFW gear unresolved; ", ""),
    if_else(garfo_conflict, "GARFO permits disagree with GFW gear; ", ""),
    if_else(roster_gear, paste0(roster_gear_change, "; "), "")), "; $")) |>
  select(-roster_gear_change)

gear_candidates |>
  count(on_removal_list, unresolved, garfo_conflict, roster_gear, wt = afe_hours,
        name = "afe_hours") |>
  left_join(count(gear_candidates, on_removal_list, unresolved, garfo_conflict, roster_gear,
                  name = "vessels"),
            by = c("on_removal_list", "unresolved", "garfo_conflict", "roster_gear"))
```

## Phase 3: Gather evidence

### GFW vessel-identity API

Looks up every Vessel ID belonging to a candidate MMSI, on either review
sheet (the gear candidates need registry gear). Parsed results are
appended to CSVs in `data/raw/vessel_evidence/{pipeline}/`, and every queried ID is
logged with the date and the GFW dataset version, so each ID is requested
once across runs. The registry records (`registryInfo`) are the independent
evidence. In pipeline v4 GFW's own label was derived largely from them; from
v5 it comes mainly from a model of the vessel's movements, with registry
records as one input. Either way a vessel typed non-fishing whose registry
lists a fishing gear is a strong false-negative candidate, and a vessel with
no registry record at all has no evidence either way.

The identity API is requested through gfwr, which always asks for the
dataset's `:latest` version. Each lookup records the version GFW served, and
the run stops if any lookup in this pipeline's cache came from another
pipeline version (e.g. a v4 cache topped up after v5 became `:latest`), since
its labels would not match this pull's.

```{r}
evid_dir <- paths$evidence
dir.create(evid_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

ev_paths <- list(
  queried  = file.path(evid_dir, "gfw_identity_queried.csv"),
  registry = file.path(evid_dir, "gfw_identity_registry.csv"),
  combined = file.path(evid_dir, "gfw_identity_combined.csv"))
# the caches' columns (queried_cols, registry_cols, combined_cols) and the API
# parsing are in r/review_helpers.R
```

```{r}
id_lookup <- bind_rows(vp, afe) |>
  filter(!is.na(MMSI), !is.na(`Vessel ID`)) |>
  distinct(vessel_id = `Vessel ID`, MMSI)

queried <- read_ev(ev_paths$queried, queried_cols)

to_query <- id_lookup |>
  filter(MMSI %in% c(candidates$MMSI, gear_candidates$MMSI),
         !vessel_id %in% queried$vessel_id[queried$status %in% c("ok", "not_found")]) |>
  pull(vessel_id) |>
  unique()

message(length(to_query), " candidate Vessel IDs not yet queried")

if (run_gfw_api && length(to_query) > 0) {
  for (ids in split(to_query, ceiling(seq_along(to_query) / api_batch_size))) {
    res <- tryCatch(
      gfw_vessel_info(search_type = "id", ids = ids,
                      key = Sys.getenv("GFW_TOKEN"), quiet = TRUE),
      error = function(e) e)

    status  <- if (inherits(res, "error")) "error" else if (is.null(res)) "not_found" else "ok"
    dataset <- NA_character_

    if (status == "ok") {
      parsed <- parse_identity(res)
      # gfwr asks for ":latest"; refuse to cache a version this pull is not
      if (!str_detect(coalesce(parsed$dataset, ""), paste0(":", paths$pipeline, "(\\.|$)"))) {
        stop("The identity API served ", parsed$dataset, ", not pipeline ", paths$pipeline,
             "; nothing from this batch was cached. Turn run_gfw_api off for this version.",
             call. = FALSE)
      }
      append_csv(parsed$registry, ev_paths$registry)
      append_csv(parsed$combined, ev_paths$combined)
      dataset <- parsed$dataset
    }

    append_csv(tibble(vessel_id = ids, queried_on = as.character(Sys.Date()),
                      status = status, dataset = dataset),
               ev_paths$queried)
    Sys.sleep(0.5)
  }
}
```

```{r}
# summarise identity evidence per MMSI
queried  <- read_ev(ev_paths$queried, queried_cols)
registry <- read_ev(ev_paths$registry, registry_cols)
combined <- read_ev(ev_paths$combined, combined_cols)

count(queried, status, dataset)

# every successful lookup must come from this pipeline version, e.g.
# "public-global-vessel-identity:v5.0" in the v5 cache
wrong_version <- queried |>
  filter(status == "ok", !str_detect(coalesce(dataset, ""), paste0(":", paths$pipeline, "(\\.|$)")))
if (nrow(wrong_version) > 0) {
  stop(nrow(wrong_version), " identity lookups in ", ev_paths$queried,
       " are not from pipeline ", paths$pipeline, ": ",
       paste(unique(wrong_version$dataset), collapse = ", "),
       ". Move them out of this version's cache before continuing.", call. = FALSE)
}

queried_mmsi <- id_lookup |>
  filter(vessel_id %in% queried$vessel_id[queried$status %in% c("ok", "not_found")]) |>
  distinct(MMSI)

# A registry record is matched to an MMSI by vessel identity, so it can belong
# to another hull: its own MMSI or call sign must agree with AIS for its gear
# to count as fishing evidence.
gfw_evidence <- queried_mmsi |>
  left_join(registry |>
              left_join(select(profiles, MMSI, call_sign), by = "MMSI") |>
              mutate(id_match = coalesce(reg_mmsi == MMSI, FALSE) |
                       coalesce(reg_callsign == call_sign, FALSE)) |>
              group_by(MMSI) |>
              summarise(reg_records  = n(),
                        reg_sources  = paste(sort(unique(source)), collapse = "|"),
                        reg_gear     = paste(sort(unique(reg_gear)), collapse = "|"),
                        reg_gear_id  = paste(sort(unique(reg_gear[id_match])), collapse = "|"),
                        reg_length_m = suppressWarnings(
                          median(as.numeric(reg_length_m), na.rm = TRUE)),
                        .groups = "drop"),
            by = "MMSI") |>
  left_join(combined |>
              group_by(MMSI) |>
              summarise(gfw_combined = paste(unique(paste0(ship, " ", year_from, "-", year_to)),
                                             collapse = "; "),
                        .groups = "drop"),
            by = "MMSI") |>
  mutate(reg_records    = coalesce(reg_records, 0L),
         reg_length_m   = if_else(is.nan(reg_length_m), NA_real_, reg_length_m),
         reg_fishing    = reg_records > 0 & has_fishing_gear(reg_gear_id),
         reg_rfmo       = reg_records > 0 & has_rfmo_source(reg_sources),
         # no fishing gear on any record, matched or not
         reg_nonfishing = reg_records > 0 & !has_fishing_gear(reg_gear) & !reg_rfmo)

count(gfw_evidence, reg_records > 0, reg_fishing, reg_rfmo)
```

## Phase 4: The review sheet

### Suggested decisions

List 1 reaches the review sheet only when there is evidence: a GFW registry
record listing fishing gear, a listing on an RFMO vessel list (e.g. ICCAT),
or a unique (or length-resolved) GARFO match with commercial or for-hire
permits. The rest of the pool cannot realistically be researched one vessel at
a time; its hours are reported below as an upper bound on what the
classification may still miss.

An ambiguous GARFO name is **resolved by length** when, of the hulls sharing
it, exactly one has a GARFO length within `screen$length_tolerance` of the GFW
registry length and permit years overlapping the vessel's AIS activity. That
hull's permits then stand in for the name's (`ambiguous_length_resolved`).
Only names matching at most `screen$max_resolve_hulls` (3) hulls are resolved:
with more, one hull can agree on length by chance.

Every row is a suggestion to check, not a classification. Accepted rows are
treated as verified and enter the Primary set, so accept only after a check
confirms that the AIS vessel (MMSI) is what the suggestion says; reject a row
that cannot be verified.

| Evidence | Suggestion | Check before accepting |
|---|---|---|
| GFW registry lists fishing gear on a record whose MMSI or call sign matches AIS (list 1) | `fishing` | MarineTraffic MMSI search shows a fishing vessel |
| On an RFMO vessel list, e.g. ICCAT, whatever the registry type (list 1) | `fishing` | A US ICCAT listing covers HMS Angling (private recreational) as well as Charter/Headboat; the MarineTraffic photo separates sport fishing boats from motor yachts |
| Unique or length-resolved GARFO match, permit years overlap (list 1) | `fishing` | The AIS vessel is the GARFO hull: PSIX call sign for the hull ID matches AIS, or the MarineTraffic MMSI search agrees. A PSIX hull lookup alone shows only that the hull is a fishing vessel |
| Charter burst, or a lease-share rise (list 2) | exclusion | Charter dates from Ørsted or the operator. On v5 pulls, read `speed_class` first (D-072). `standby-like`: fits safety or guard work (`Operation` is pre-filled `Safety`). `underway`: most of its Stage 3 AFE is at fishing speed, as for NICHOLAS C, a trawler the screen flagged for working the leases. Check its GARFO permits and MarineTraffic, and without charter evidence accept it as `fishing` with `activity_excluded` FALSE and no window |
| GFW registry lists non-fishing gear, or name or behaviour only (list 3) | `non_fishing` | MarineTraffic MMSI search; a unique GARFO match is noted as contrary evidence |
| Battery-level call sign (list 4) | `gear_marker` | |
| MMSI not 9 digits only (list 4) | `unknown` | Whether it is a vessel |
| Counted as fishing in the previous pipeline version, retyped in this one (list 5) | `fishing` | As for list 1: MarineTraffic MMSI search, PSIX, the GARFO match if any. Reject when the new label is right (e.g. a yacht or a recreational boat the analysis does not count as fishing) |

Charter windows are suggested from the first and last Stage 3 day with lease
activity; replace them with Ørsted's dates where available.

This sheet covers hull and activity only. Gear is set on the gear review
sheet (below); a missed fishing vessel you accept here appears there on the
next run, since GFW's gear for it is unresolved.

```{r}
evidence_cols <- c("list", "reason", "names", "flag", "call_sign", "vp_hours",
                   "s1", "s2", "s3", "afe_hours", "h_day", "lease_share",
                   "lease_share_s12", "lease_share_s3",
                   # charter speed check (D-072; v5 pulls on)
                   "speed_class", "afe_speed_h", "afe_lt2", "afe_lt4", "afe_median_kn",
                   "reg_records",
                   "reg_sources", "reg_gear", "gfw_combined", "reg_length_m",
                   "garfo_class", "garfo_hull_id", "hull_is_uscg",
                   "garfo_permits", "garfo_years", "garfo_length_ft",
                   "garfo_home_port", "garfo_permit_type", "garfo_gear_hint",
                   "garfo_oa_permits", "garfo_oa_directed", "garfo_categories",
                   "garfo_max_hulls_with_name", "garfo_max_mmsi_with_name",
                   "psix_link", "psix_hull", "psix_ais_call_sign")

# Ambiguous GARFO names resolved by length: exactly one of the hulls sharing
# the name agrees with the registry length, and its permit years overlap the
# MMSI's AIS activity. Common names (more than screen$max_resolve_hulls hulls)
# are left ambiguous, since one of many hulls can agree on length by chance.
garfo_resolved <- garfo_by_hull |>
  filter(MMSI %in% profiles$MMSI[profiles$garfo_match %in% "ambiguous" &
                                   profiles$garfo_hulls <= screen$max_resolve_hulls]) |>
  inner_join(gfw_evidence |> filter(!is.na(reg_length_m)) |> select(MMSI, reg_length_m),
             by = "MMSI") |>
  mutate(agree = length_agrees(garfo_length_ft, reg_length_m, screen$length_tolerance)) |>
  group_by(MMSI) |>
  filter(sum(agree) == 1, agree, year_overlap) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(garfo_match = "ambiguous_length_resolved") |>
  select(MMSI, garfo_match, garfo_years, garfo_hull_id, hull_is_uscg, garfo_permits,
         garfo_sources, garfo_length_ft, garfo_home_port, garfo_categories,
         garfo_oa_permits, garfo_oa_directed, garfo_n_oa, garfo_permit_type,
         garfo_oa_bundle, garfo_gear_hint)

# replace a resolved MMSI's GARFO summary (all hulls with the name) with its
# hull's; garfo_hulls keeps the number of hulls the name matched
apply_resolved <- function(df) {
  rows_update(df, garfo_resolved, by = "MMSI", unmatched = "ignore")
}

count(garfo_resolved, garfo_permit_type)

assessed <- candidates |>
  apply_resolved() |>
  left_join(gfw_evidence, by = "MMSI") |>
  mutate(
    across(c(reg_fishing, reg_rfmo, reg_nonfishing), \(x) coalesce(x, FALSE)),
    garfo_match = coalesce(garfo_match, "none"),

    length_known = !is.na(reg_length_m) & !is.na(garfo_length_ft),
    length_agree = length_agrees(garfo_length_ft, reg_length_m, screen$length_tolerance),
    garfo_class = case_when(
      garfo_match == "unique_years" & length_agree ~ "unique_years_length",
      garfo_match == "unique_years" & length_known ~ "length_conflict",
      TRUE                                         ~ garfo_match),
    # a recreational-only permit is not evidence of a fishing vessel
    garfo_support = garfo_class %in% c("unique_years_length", "unique_years",
                                       "ambiguous_length_resolved") &
                    !garfo_permit_type %in% c("recreational only", "unmapped codes only"),
    has_evidence = reg_fishing | reg_rfmo | garfo_support)
```

### USCG PSIX checks

A GARFO match links a hull to an MMSI by name only. The USCG Port State
Information Exchange (PSIX, on CGMIX) ties a USCG official number (the numeric
GARFO hull ID) to a call sign and a service type, and the AIS call sign to an
official number, so it can test whether the AIS vessel is the GARFO hull.
Lookups go through PSIX's public web service and are cached in
`data/raw/vessel_evidence/psix_lookups.csv`, one row per vessel returned, so
each hull ID and call sign is requested once across runs. They run only with
`run_psix_api: true`.

Two lookups are made for vessels that reach the review sheet (list 1 with
evidence, and list 3): the GARFO hull ID, when it is a USCG official number,
and the AIS call sign, when the vessel is US-flagged and the call sign has a US
format. `psix_link` records the outcome:

| `psix_link` | Meaning | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `match` | The AIS call sign is the hull's PSIX call sign, or looks up to the hull's official number | Hull identity confirmed; the PSIX service type still has to fit (a whale-watch boat and a headboat are both inspected passenger vessels) |
| `ais_is_other_hull` | The AIS call sign looks up to a different official number | GARFO match not used |
| `call_sign_differs` | The hull's PSIX call sign differs from the AIS call sign | Note only: the call sign may have changed when a licence was reissued, or the MMSI may be another boat with the name |
| `hull_has_cs_ais_none` | The hull has a call sign in PSIX but AIS broadcasts none | Note only: check that the MMSI is that hull (it may be another boat with the name) |
| `hull_not_found` | The official number is not in PSIX | Note only |
| `no_link` | Neither side has a call sign to compare | Note only |
| `not_queried` | A lookup is still missing from the cache | Run with `run_psix_api: true` |

A `match` whose PSIX service type is not fishing, passenger or recreational
(e.g. research, towing, freight) also stops the GARFO match from being used. A
GARFO match that is not used no longer counts as list-1 evidence. A vessel
with no other evidence then leaves the review sheet, and its GARFO permits are
not used for its gear hint or permit group. `psix_hull` and
`psix_ais_call_sign` give what PSIX returned for each side. They also show
when the AIS vessel's PSIX name differs from its AIS name.

```{r}
psix_path <- paths$psix # shared by every pipeline version: PSIX is USCG, not GFW

psix_targets <- assessed |>
  filter((list == "1_missed_fishing" & has_evidence) | list == "3_nonfishing_typed_fishing") |>
  psix_keys()

psix <- read_ev(psix_path, psix_cols)

to_psix <- bind_rows(
  tibble(key_type = "call_sign",   key = psix_targets$ais_cs),
  tibble(key_type = "official_no", key = psix_targets$hull)) |>
  filter(!is.na(key)) |>
  distinct() |>
  anti_join(filter(psix, status %in% c("ok", "not_found")), by = c("key_type", "key"))

message(nrow(to_psix), " PSIX lookups not yet made")

if (run_psix_api && nrow(to_psix) > 0) {
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(to_psix))) {
    k   <- to_psix[i, ]
    res <- tryCatch(
      if (k$key_type == "call_sign") psix_query(call_sign = k$key)
      else psix_query(official_no = k$key),
      error = function(e) e)

    status <- if (inherits(res, "error")) "error" else if (is.null(res)) "not_found" else "ok"
    out <- (if (status == "ok") res else tibble(psix_official_no = NA_character_)) |>
      mutate(key_type = k$key_type, key = k$key,
             queried_on = as.character(Sys.Date()), status = status)
    out[setdiff(psix_cols, names(out))] <- NA_character_
    append_csv(select(out, all_of(psix_cols)), psix_path)
    Sys.sleep(1)
  }
  psix <- read_ev(psix_path, psix_cols)
}

count(psix, key_type, status)
```

```{r}
psix_checks <- psix_evaluate(psix_targets, psix)

count(psix_checks, psix_link, psix_contradicts)

# re-running this chunk interactively replaces, rather than duplicates, the columns
psix_add <- c("psix_link", "psix_hull", "psix_ais_call_sign", "psix_contradicts", "psix_note")
assessed <- assessed |>
  select(-any_of(psix_add)) |>
  left_join(select(psix_checks, MMSI, all_of(psix_add)), by = "MMSI") |>
  mutate(psix_contradicts = coalesce(psix_contradicts, FALSE),
         garfo_support = garfo_support & !psix_contradicts,
         has_evidence  = reg_fishing | reg_rfmo | garfo_support)

# MMSIs whose GARFO match PSIX contradicts: no GARFO gear hint or permit group
psix_not_hull <- assessed$MMSI[assessed$psix_contradicts]

# list-1 vessels that leave the review sheet because PSIX contradicts their
# only evidence
assessed |>
  filter(list == "1_missed_fishing", psix_contradicts, !has_evidence) |>
  select(MMSI, names, call_sign, garfo_hull_id, psix_note)
```

### Build the review sheet

```{r}
review <- assessed |>
  # list 1 is reviewed only where there is evidence; list 5 always is
  filter(list != "1_missed_fishing" | has_evidence) |>
  mutate(
    decision    = NA_character_,
    decided_on  = NA_character_,
    Vessel_Name = names,
    hull_class = case_when(
      list == "4_gear_marker" & str_detect(reason, "battery") ~ "gear_marker",
      list == "4_gear_marker"                                 ~ "unknown",
      list == "1_missed_fishing"                              ~ "fishing",
      list == "2_charter_activity"                            ~ "fishing",
      list == "3_nonfishing_typed_fishing"                    ~ "non_fishing",
      list == "5_roster_label_change"                         ~ "fishing"),
    activity_excluded = as.character(list == "2_charter_activity"),
    valid_from = if_else(list == "2_charter_activity",
                         as.character(s3_lease_first), NA_character_),
    valid_to   = if_else(list == "2_charter_activity",
                         as.character(s3_lease_last), NA_character_),
    # a standby-like charter candidate is suggested as safety work (D-072)
    Operation  = if_else(list == "2_charter_activity" & speed_class %in% "standby-like",
                         "Safety", NA_character_),
    Identified_By = case_when(
      list == "1_missed_fishing" & reg_fishing              ~ "gfw_registry",
      list == "1_missed_fishing" & reg_rfmo                 ~ "gfw_registry_rfmo",
      list == "1_missed_fishing" & garfo_support            ~ "garfo_name_match",
      list == "3_nonfishing_typed_fishing" & reg_nonfishing ~ "gfw_registry",
      list == "2_charter_activity"                          ~ "behavioural_screen",
      list == "4_gear_marker"                               ~ "mmsi_format_screen",
      list == "5_roster_label_change"                       ~ paste0(prev_pipeline, "_roster_check"),
      TRUE                                                  ~ "screen"),
    evidence_ref = if_else(garfo_support,
                           paste0("GARFO hull ", garfo_hull_id, "; permit ", garfo_permits),
                           NA_character_),
    pull_date = as.character(pull_date),
    gfw_pipeline = paths$pipeline, # GFW pipeline version of this pull
    hms_chb   = str_detect(coalesce(garfo_categories, ""), fixed("HMS:CHARTER/HEADBOAT")),
    Notes = paste0(
      case_when(
        garfo_support & hull_is_uscg %in% TRUE &
          (is.na(psix_link) | psix_link %in% "not_queried") ~ paste0(
          reason, ". To confirm: look up USCG official no. ", garfo_hull_id,
          " in CGMIX PSIX; its call sign should be ", coalesce(call_sign, "(none in AIS)"),
          ". GARFO permits: ", garfo_permit_type),
        garfo_support & hull_is_uscg %in% TRUE ~ paste0(
          reason, ". GARFO permits: ", garfo_permit_type),
        garfo_support ~ paste0(
          reason, ". State-registered hull ", garfo_hull_id,
          "; cannot be linked to a call sign. GARFO permits: ", garfo_permit_type),
        list == "3_nonfishing_typed_fishing" & garfo_match == "unique_years" &
          !psix_contradicts ~ paste0(
          reason, ". Note: unique GARFO permit match suggests a fishing vessel"),
        TRUE ~ reason),
      if_else(!is.na(psix_note), paste0(". ", psix_note), ""),
      if_else(garfo_support & garfo_class == "ambiguous_length_resolved",
              paste0(". GARFO name matches ", garfo_hulls,
                     " hulls; only this one agrees with the registry length"), ""),
      if_else(list == "1_missed_fishing" & reg_rfmo, paste0(
        ". On an RFMO vessel list (", reg_sources, "), registry gear ", reg_gear, "; ",
        case_when(
          hms_chb & garfo_support ~ "GARFO HMS Charter/Headboat permit: for-hire",
          hms_chb ~ "a GARFO hull with this name holds an HMS Charter/Headboat permit",
          TRUE    ~ "no GARFO HMS Charter/Headboat match: may be HMS Angling (private recreational)")),
        ""),
      # the charter speed check (D-072), on pulls with speed
      if_else(list == "2_charter_activity" & !is.na(speed_class), paste0(
        ". Speed check: ", speed_class, " (", round(100 * coalesce(afe_lt4, 0)),
        "% of ", round(afe_speed_h), " Stage 3 AFE h on days < 4 kn, ",
        round(100 * coalesce(afe_lt2, 0)), "% < 2 kn; median ",
        round(afe_median_kn, 1), " kn)",
        if_else(speed_class %in% "underway",
                ". Check GARFO permits before accepting an exclusion", "")),
        ""))) |>
  # within each list: GFW registry evidence first, then RFMO listings, then
  # GARFO hulls PSIX ties to the AIS call sign, then by hours; list 5 by its
  # fishing-effort hours in the previous version. Charter candidates (list 2)
  # come standby-like first, then mixed, too few hours and underway (D-072).
  mutate(speed_rank = coalesce(match(speed_class, c("standby-like", "mixed",
                                                    "too few hours", "underway")), 0L)) |>
  arrange(list, desc(coalesce(afe_hours_old, 0)), speed_rank,
          desc(reg_fishing), desc(reg_rfmo),
          desc(psix_link %in% "match"), desc(vp_hours)) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 3))) |>
  select(all_of(decision_cols), any_of(evidence_cols))
```

### Write the review sheet

The sheet is regenerated every run; anything you mark in it is collected into
`vessel_decisions.csv` at the start of the next run (Phase 1).

```{r}
dir.create(paths$review, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
write_csv(review, review_path, na = "")

count(review, list)
```

### What is left unreviewed

List 1 vessels without evidence are not reviewed. Their hours bound what the
classification could still be missing; report them alongside the results.

Most of list 1 is offshore wind, supply and survey traffic, so its share of
*all* VP hours is large and says little about fishing. VP is shown instead as
a share of GFW `FISHING` VP, the population the analysis starts from. The AFE
share is near zero by construction (GFW computes effort only for vessels it
treats as fishing), so it does not bound missed fishing; the VP share does.
Vessels whose GFW registry records list no fishing gear are split from those
with no registry record, but a registry type of PASSENGER is weak evidence
against: sport fishing boats are often typed that way.

```{r}
fishing_vp <- sum(profiles$vp_hours[profiles$gfw_vessel_type %in% "FISHING"])

unreviewed <- assessed |>
  filter(list == "1_missed_fishing") |>
  mutate(evidence = case_when(
    has_evidence     ~ "for fishing (reviewed)",
    psix_contradicts ~ "GARFO match contradicted by PSIX",
    reg_nonfishing   ~ "registry, no fishing gear",
    TRUE             ~ "none either way"))

unreviewed |>
  group_by(evidence) |>
  summarise(vessels = n(),
            vp_share_of_fishing = round(sum(vp_hours) / fishing_vp, 4),
            vp_share_of_all     = round(sum(vp_hours) / total_vp, 4),
            afe_share           = round(sum(afe_hours) / total_afe, 4),
            .groups = "drop")

# The residual by GFW type: unreviewed PASSENGER and OTHER vessels are where
# recreational and for-hire boats with no registry or GARFO evidence remain.
# Their VP share of FISHING VP bounds the missed recreational and for-hire
# presence; report it with the results.
unreviewed |>
  filter(!has_evidence) |>
  group_by(evidence, gfw_vessel_type, call_sign = !is.na(call_sign)) |>
  summarise(vessels = n(),
            vp_share_of_fishing = round(sum(vp_hours) / fishing_vp, 4),
            vp_hours = round(sum(vp_hours)),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(evidence, desc(vp_hours))

# unreviewed vessels with any apparent fishing hours
unreviewed |>
  filter(!has_evidence, afe_hours > 0) |>
  arrange(desc(afe_hours)) |>
  select(MMSI, names, gfw_vessel_type, flag, vp_hours, afe_hours, evidence,
         garfo_class)
```

### The gear review sheet

One row per gear candidate (Phase 2): removal-list fishing vessels first, then
the rest by fishing-effort hours. The suggested `gear_class` comes from a
unique (or length-resolved) GARFO match's permits if there is one, otherwise
from the GFW registry gear (after the API run), otherwise `POLE_AND_LINE` for
a vessel on an RFMO list such as ICCAT, otherwise it is blank.

| GARFO permits | Suggested gear class |
|---|---|
| For-hire only | `POLE_AND_LINE` |
| For-hire plus `screen$oa_bundle_min` or more open-access commercial permits -- the bundle party boats typically hold | `POLE_AND_LINE`, but treat it as `possible` |
| For-hire plus fewer open-access commercial permits | blank -- the vessel may fish commercially on some trips (e.g. Handgear B, tilefish); the note lists the directed open-access permits |
| For-hire plus limited-access commercial permits | blank |
| Commercial: trap permits only (lobster trap areas, red crab, a trap limit) | `FIXED` |
| Commercial: dredge or trawl permits only (scallop, clam, squid trawl) | `MOBILE` |
| Anything else | blank |

`garfo_gear_hint` and `garfo_categories` are shown even when the GARFO match
is ambiguous, as information. A vessel gets one gear class per window, so a
dual-permitted vessel that alternates charter and commercial trips is
misclassified for some of its trips whichever class is chosen; Phase 6
reports these vessels as a separate group.

```{r}
gear_evidence_cols <- c("gear_reason", "gfw_class", "garfo_match", "garfo_gear_hint",
                        "garfo_permit_type", "garfo_mmsi_sequence", "garfo_categories",
                        "garfo_hull_id", "reg_records", "reg_gear", "names",
                        "vp_hours", "afe_hours", "s1", "s2", "s3")

# GARFO hulls PSIX says are not the AIS vessel, from cached lookups only (an
# accepted vessel was looked up while it was on the hull review sheet)
gear_psix <- gear_candidates |> apply_resolved() |> psix_keys() |> psix_evaluate(psix)
not_hull  <- union(psix_not_hull, gear_psix$MMSI[gear_psix$psix_contradicts])

gear_review <- gear_candidates |>
  apply_resolved() |>
  left_join(select(gfw_evidence, MMSI, reg_records, reg_gear, reg_rfmo), by = "MMSI") |>
  mutate(
    garfo_hint  = if_else(garfo_match %in% c("unique_years", "ambiguous_length_resolved") &
                            !MMSI %in% not_hull,
                          garfo_gear_hint, NA_character_),
    reg_hint    = reg_gear_class(reg_gear),
    # an RFMO-listed (e.g. ICCAT) vessel with no gear evidence is a sport or
    # for-hire boat fishing for tunas and other highly migratory species
    rfmo_hint   = if_else(reg_rfmo %in% TRUE, "POLE_AND_LINE", NA_character_),
    decision    = NA_character_,
    decided_on  = NA_character_,
    valid_from  = NA_character_,
    valid_to    = NA_character_,
    Vessel_Name = names,
    gear_class  = coalesce(garfo_hint, reg_hint, rfmo_hint),
    basis = case_when(!is.na(garfo_hint) ~ "GARFO permit",
                      !is.na(reg_hint)   ~ "GFW registry",
                      !is.na(rfmo_hint)  ~ "RFMO listing",
                      TRUE               ~ NA_character_),
    evidence_ref = if_else(!is.na(garfo_hint),
                           paste0("GARFO hull ", garfo_hull_id, "; permit ", garfo_permits),
                           NA_character_),
    pull_date = as.character(pull_date),
    gfw_pipeline = paths$pipeline, # GFW pipeline version of this pull
    Notes = paste0(
      gear_reason,
      if_else(!is.na(garfo_hint) & !is.na(reg_hint) & garfo_hint != reg_hint,
              paste0(". GFW registry gear suggests ", reg_hint, " instead"), ""),
      case_when(
        garfo_oa_bundle %in% TRUE ~ paste0(
          ". Holds ", garfo_n_oa, " open-access commercial permits, a typical party-boat",
          " bundle; POLE_AND_LINE suggested -- treat it as possible"),
        garfo_permit_type %in% "for-hire + open-access commercial" ~ paste0(
          ". Also holds open-access commercial permits (directed: ",
          if_else(garfo_oa_directed %in% "", "none", garfo_oa_directed),
          "); may fish commercially on some trips"),
        TRUE ~ ""))) |>
  arrange(desc(on_removal_list), desc(afe_hours)) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 3))) |>
  select(all_of(gear_cols), any_of(gear_evidence_cols))

write_csv(gear_review, gear_review_path, na = "")

count(gear_review, basis, gear_class)
```

## Phase 5: Permit groups for the analysis

Vessels whose GARFO permits combine for-hire with commercial permits
(`commercial + for-hire`, `for-hire + open-access commercial`) may fish both
ways, on different trips. A single gear class cannot represent them, so
`04_classify_aggregate.qmd` reports their hours as a separate group and checks
whether the Stage 2 → 3 change holds without them. Only unique,
year-overlapping GARFO matches that PSIX does not contradict get a group; every
other MMSI is `no unique GARFO match` in 04.

The groups are written to `references/vessel_permit_groups_{pipeline}.csv` so that 04 can
run without the GARFO files. Only the MMSI and the permit group are written;
no GARFO hull, permit number or owner field leaves this step.

```{r}
permit_groups <- profiles |>
  filter(garfo_match == "unique_years", !MMSI %in% not_hull) |>
  transmute(MMSI, permit_group = garfo_permit_type, pull_date = as.character(pull_date)) |>
  arrange(MMSI)

write_csv(permit_groups, paths$permit_groups, na = "")

count(permit_groups, permit_group)
```

### Snapshot the fishing roster

GFW reprocesses its data between pipeline versions and relabels vessels. A
vessel counted as fishing here only because GFW typed it FISHING (most of
them: they have no crosswalk row) would silently leave the Strict and Primary
sets if a later version retyped it. The roster records every MMSI that counted
as fishing in this pull, by any source (GFW type, crosswalk fishing hull, gear
correction, fishing GARFO permit group), with its labels, gear class, Primary
membership and hours by stage. The next version's run compares its labels with
this file and sends the changes to review
(`planning/gfw_pipeline_v5_plan.qmd`, Sections 2.7 and 3.6).

It is written **once per pipeline version** and never replaced: render with
`-P write_roster:true` once, then commit the file. The chunk stops if
`references/` has uncommitted changes after this run's writes, so that the
roster always matches a commit of the crosswalk and decisions it was built
from.

```{r}
roster_path <- sprintf(paths$roster, paths$pipeline)

if (isTRUE(qparams$write_roster)) {
  # this run has just rewritten the crosswalk, permit groups and (if any rows
  # were marked) the decision files; they must equal what is committed
  ref_status <- system2("git", c("status", "--porcelain", "--", "references/"),
                        stdout = TRUE)
  if (length(ref_status) > 0) {
    stop("references/ has uncommitted changes; commit them before writing the ",
         "roster:\n  ", paste(ref_status, collapse = "\n  "), call. = FALSE)
  }
  head_commit <- system2("git", c("rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"), stdout = TRUE)

  roster <- build_fishing_roster(vp, afe, cw, gear, permit_groups, gfw_labels,
                                 pull_date, pipeline = paths$pipeline,
                                 source_commit = head_commit)
  write_roster_once(roster, roster_path)
} else if (file.exists(roster_path)) {
  roster <- read_chr(roster_path)
  message("Roster for ", paths$pipeline, " already written: ", roster_path)
} else {
  roster <- NULL
  message("No roster for ", paths$pipeline,
          " yet; render once with -P write_roster:true")
}

# what is on the roster, and why (an MMSI can have several sources)
if (!is.null(roster)) {
  roster |>
    mutate(across(starts_with("src_") | any_of("in_primary"), as.logical)) |>
    summarise(mmsi = n(),
              across(starts_with("src_"), sum),
              in_primary = sum(in_primary))
}
```

## Phase 6: Repeatability checks

### GFW label drift

GFW's labels change between pulls (CYGNUS was typed FISHING/INCONCLUSIVE in an
earlier pull and CARGO in the 2026-10-06 pull). Any decided vessel whose
current label differs from the one recorded when the decision was made is
listed here for a second look.

```{r}
decisions |>
  filter(!is.na(gfw_vessel_type)) |>
  distinct(MMSI, Vessel_Name, gfw_vessel_type, gfw_gear_type, pull_date) |>
  left_join(gfw_labels, by = "MMSI", suffix = c("_recorded", "_current")) |>
  filter(is.na(gfw_vessel_type_current) |
           gfw_vessel_type_recorded != gfw_vessel_type_current |
           gfw_gear_type_recorded != gfw_gear_type_current)
```

### Label drift across the roster

On a run against a new pipeline version, the same check for every vessel on
the previous version's roster, decided or not (Phase 1). **Type drift** is a
change of GFW vessel type; unprotected ones in the previous Primary set are
list 5 of the review sheet. **Gear-only drift** is a change of gear class
with the same vessel type; unprotected ones are on the gear review sheet.
Protected changes are settled by an existing crosswalk row or gear
correction. The hours are the previous version's.

```{r}
if (!is.null(roster_chk)) {
  type_mmsi <- roster_chk$MMSI[roster_chk$change == "type"]
  roster_chk |>
    filter(change != "missing") |>
    mutate(drift = case_when(change == "type" ~ "type",
                             !MMSI %in% type_mmsi ~ "gear only",
                             TRUE ~ "gear, with a type change")) |>
    group_by(drift, protected, in_primary) |>
    summarise(vessels = n(), vp_hours_old = round(sum(vp_hours_old)),
              afe_hours_old = round(sum(afe_hours_old)), .groups = "drop")
}
```

```{r}
# gear-only drift: the transitions between gear classes
if (!is.null(roster_chk)) {
  roster_chk |>
    filter(change == "gear_class", !MMSI %in% type_mmsi) |>
    count(protected, class_old, class_new, name = "vessels", sort = TRUE)
}
```

### Roster vessels missing from this pull

Roster vessels with no records in this pull's analysis window. A pipeline
version can drop records (e.g. v5 removes port false positives) or split a
vessel's identity, so check the hours before reading anything into them.
Report only; there is nothing to decide.

```{r}
if (!is.null(roster_chk)) {
  missing_roster <- roster_chk |> filter(change == "missing")
  # an if block shows only its last value, so the summary is printed
  print(missing_roster |>
    group_by(in_primary) |>
    summarise(vessels = n(), vp_hours_old = round(sum(vp_hours_old)),
              afe_hours_old = round(sum(afe_hours_old)), .groups = "drop"))
  missing_roster |>
    arrange(desc(vp_hours_old)) |>
    select(MMSI, Vessel_Name, in_primary, type_old, gear_old, vp_hours_old, afe_hours_old)
}
```
